_comment: Wiring example for Claude Code. Copy the `hooks` block into your
.claude/settings.json and adjust paths to where you put this repo.
Two conventions here are load-bearing rather than stylistic:
1. Hooks are invoked via $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, never an absolute path. That
variable is set in the hook execution environment and resolves to the
project root on every machine. A drive letter or a home directory in this
file is a hook that silently no-ops for everyone but its author.
2. Note which hooks are wrapped in `|| true` and which are NOT. The wrapper
discards the hook's exit code. That is correct for an advisory hook and
WRONG for a blocking one -- a fail-closed check whose exit code is thrown
away is not fail-closed, it is decorative. The blocking hooks here signal
a denial through stdout JSON (permissionDecision: deny) at exit 0 for
exactly this reason, so they survive the wrapper either way. Suppressing
stderr with 2>/dev/null has the same shape of hazard: a hook that exits 0
is not read for its stderr, and its plain stdout is not shown to the model
for most events. A message that must reach someone belongs in the JSON
output (the deny reason, or the event's context/message field), not in
free text that is discarded along with the noise you meant to suppress.
3. Every entry carries an explicit `timeout` (seconds). Without one the
harness default applies, and a hook that runs past its timeout is treated
as a non-blocking error -- for a fail-closed guard that means ALLOW. Size
the guards' bound well above their slowest real run on a loaded machine;
the advisory hooks can be tighter.
tests/run-all.sh reads THIS file to derive wiring coverage -- which wired
hooks have a test file. Point it at your own settings to get the same
report for your live layer:
WIRING=~/.claude/settings.json bash tests/run-all.sh
